Darnell Hillman.
Darnell "Dr. Dunk" Hillman was born on August 29, 1949.
Darnell Hillman is a former professional basketball player.
Darnell Hillman graduated from Hiram W. Johnson High School.
Darnell Hillman's height is 6 ft 9 in (2.06 m).
Darnell Hillman played college basketball at San Jose State University.
Darnell Hillman was selected in the first round of the 1971 NBA draft as the 8th pick overall by the Golden State Warriors.
Darnell Hillman opted to play for the Indiana Pacers instead of the Golden State Warriors.
Darnell Hillman branched out into track and field at San Jose State University.
Darnell Hillman cleared 6'11 1/2" in high jump, which ranks 10th on San Jose's all-time list.
Darnell Hillman played six seasons for the Indiana Pacers.
The Indiana Pacers joined the NBA with the ABA–NBA merger in June 1976.
Darnell Hillman earned a reputation for his stylish slam dunks and oversized afro hairstyle.
Darnell Hillman won the NBA's Slam Dunk Contest in the 1976–77 season.
Darnell Hillman was not officially given an official trophy for winning the NBA's Slam Dunk Contest until March 8, 2017.
Darnell Hillman defeated Larry McNeill of the Golden State Warriors in the final of the NBA's Slam Dunk Contest.
At the time of the NBA's Slam Dunk Contest final, Darnell Hillman's rights had been traded to the New York Nets.
Darnell Hillman did not yet sign a contract with any team at the time of the NBA's Slam Dunk Contest.
Darnell Hillman competed in a plain white tank top during the NBA's Slam Dunk Contest.

For the post-competition interview, Darnell Hillman wore a shirt with "Bottle Shoppe" – the name of an Indianapolis liquor store that sponsored a city parks softball league team for which he played left field.
Darnell Hillman later played with the New Jersey Nets in the NBA.
Darnell Hillman later played with the Denver Nuggets in the NBA.
Darnell Hillman later played with the Kansas City Kings in the NBA.
Darnell Hillman later played with the Golden State Warriors in the NBA.
Darnell Hillman ended his career in 1980 with combined NBA/ABA totals of 6,666 points and 5,187 rebounds during the regular season.
Darnell Hillman ended his career in 1980 with combined NBA/ABA totals of 7,339 points and 5,809 rebounds including post-season.
Darnell Hillman played for the United States men's national basketball team at the 1970 FIBA World Championship.
Darnell Hillman was asked by a reporter if he could jump high enough to grab a quarter off the top of the backboard; responded with "Put a $100 bill up there and see."
The reporter declined Darnell Hillman's offer after hearing stories about him picking quarters off the top of backboards.
Darnell Hillman won the "Biggest ABA Afro" Award at the 1997 ABA reunion.
Currently, Darnell Hillman serves as Associate Director of Camps, Clinics & Alumni Relations for the Indiana Pacers.
On February 4, 2012, Darnell Hillman's #45 jersey was retired by San Jose State University.
Darnell Hillman is one of only three Spartans to have their jerseys retired at San Jose State University.
